evidence.reasoning: Source shows: *name = wmem_alloc(pool, 256); buddyname_length = tvb_get_ntohs(tvb, offset); if (pool) memcpy(*name, tvb_get_ptr(tvb, offset, 1), buddyname_length); No bounds check ties buddyname_length to 256, so if attacker controls the 16-bit length, memcpy can overflow the 256-byte heap buffer. Also tvb_get_ptr(tvb, offset, 1) only guarantees 1 byte is available at offset; memcpy then reads buddyname_length bytes from that pointer, so it can over-read the tvb backing buffer (though tvb_get_ptr may return a pointer into a contiguous buffer; the over-read would be caught by ASan if it crosses into poisoned memory). The only guard is `if (pool)` which is not a clamp; pool is non-NULL in normal use. Reachability confirmed by check_reachability. A reach_probe could not be executed due to missing ASan binary path in the environment, so no runtime crash evidence was gathered here.

Additionally, it obtains the source pointer with tvb_get_ptr(..., 1) (only 1 byte ensured) and then reads buddyname_length bytes, risking tvb buffer over-read.

Trigger requires buddyname_length > 256 (and/or > available tvb bytes) and pool non-NULL.

args.generator_code:
def generate()->bytes:
    # Try to craft an AIM message where buddyname_length is large.
    # We don't know full framing; use a generic strategy: emit many bytes with
    # a 0xFFFF length early, hoping handler_aim parses it as buddyname_length.
    data = bytearray(b"AIM\x00")
    # pad
    data += b"\x00"*16
    # put 0xFFFF in big-endian
    data += b"\xff\xff"
    # add some payload bytes
    data += b"B"*1024
    return bytes(data)

full_messages.content:
You are a vulnerability verifier. All candidate functions are already
reachable from the fuzzer — do NOT re-litigate reachability as pass/fail. Your job
is to gather EVIDENCE about whether the reached code actually contains a
crashing memory-safety bug of the stated type, then submit it.

Gather evidence with the tools:
- read_function(name): read the real source.
- check_reachability(function_name): confirm the call graph (depth, direct/indirect).
- reach_probe(generator_code, target): write Python `def generate()->bytes` that
  produces an input aiming to REACH `target` (a function name or "file.c:LINE").
  It runs the input on the real ASan binary under gdb and tells you whether the
  target was reached and whether it crashed. A crash is proof; a reach grounds
  your judgment. Only a real crash or reach can raise the score above the ceiling —
  you cannot assert a high score from reading alone.
- submit_evidence(...): report your structured findings (see its schema). Call it
  once, last.

Two of the fields are NOT about scoring — they correct the SP for the downstream
PoV stage, and you are the right one to write them because you just read the real
code (and maybe ran a reach_probe):
- corrected_description: if the SP's stated bug type/description is wrong or
  imprecise given the real code, write the accurate one (else restate it).
- control_flow_to_bug: the real path from the fuzzer entry to the crash site — the
  key functions, branches, and conditions that must hold to trigger it.

Do NOT pass things "when in doubt". Report what the evidence shows. Absence of a
crash is not proof of safety; a proven clamp/guard on the tainted value IS
disconfirming.

Verify this suspicious point.

Fuzzer: handler_aim   Sanitizer: address
Function: aim_get_buddyname
Claimed bug type: ABRT
Suspicious-point description (from the finder — may be imprecise): `*name = wmem_alloc(pool, 256)` then `memcpy(*name, tvb_get_ptr(tvb, offset, 1), buddyname_length)` copies `buddyname_length` (a 16-bit value, up to 65535) from a 1-byte tvb pointer into the 256-byte buffer -- both a heap overflow and a tvb over-read that ASan aborts on.

Control flow to the bug:
  - handler_aim; aim_get_buddyname reads buddyname_length = tvb_get_ntohs(...)
  - memcpy(*name, tvb_get_ptr(tvb, offset, 1), buddyname_length) with length up to 65535
  - 256-byte buffer overflow + tvb over-read -> ASan abort

The function is reachable (confirm with check_reachability if useful).

Read the function, judge whether a fuzzer input can drive a ABRT
there, optionally reach_probe a candidate input to ground it, then submit_evidence.
